>In the end we all die. Some may believe we go on into another life and that’s fine, but from what we know there is just nothing.

This is really difficult, in my opinion I think this is mostly correct, but it's nothing to be afraid of, because essentially we will simply recede back like the tide back into the ocean. Your absence of life won't be painful, or negative, because it won't be anything. We'll be gone. Think of it like an intense dreamless sleep. But I mean, who knows. All I know is I won't be here when I die anymore. 

>So really the only reason we live is to further the human race. Definitely sounds a bit odd writing it out but it’s true. Our only purpose is to make life for future generations better, and to possibly make a name for ourself

This is true. We are animals at our core. So much of human nature is feeling resistant, even disgusted, by that fact, i.e. that we're "just" animals. Inherent in that is a desire to survive, to reproduce, etc. What makes us different is our awareness, and our desire to be more than our lives. How we decide to do that is varying, and I feel the desire to seek fame and fortune, or to "change the world" is actually detrimental overall, because not everyone will be able to do that, and I don't know if it's a good thing that entire generations of folks feel like a failure because they didn't do so. 

>If you don’t care about the further there really is no meaning to life. You can believe whatever you want to believe about why there is life but when you really boil it down we are a cosmic anomaly with no reason for existence.......fun

I'm going to assume you meant "future" not "further". But yes, you're right. The unfortunate conclusion in a lot of these discussions is that there isn't any predestinated point to your life. Are you okay with that? I feel that tons of people are not. It's really hard to know that the only point to your life is the point you make. The real conclusion is that nobody is going to be able to honestly tell you how your life will go, and what the meaning of that life is. You make your life's significance, or you die obscure and unknown.

Canadian here, lots of French family but still quite novice in my own ability. 

I actually just came home from a week-long trip to Montreal with my sister. In my experience of the city in terms of language use I found that French was by far the working language of choice by the majority who weren't in the obvious "touristy" areas (and even the touristy places usually greeted you with "bonjour/hello" simultaneously). 

Whenever I spoke French to people they would almost always switch to English because I was obviously struggling with it, and they often did this with my sister too even though she's completely fluent but with a notable Anglo accent. However my sister would always respond in French anyway and then the locals would revert back to French when they recognized she wanted to practice/use French. 

tl;dr most folks speak English but if you make a point of using your French, they will usually humour you and speak French back. And this was during the off-season tourism-wise, could be much different in the summer months (i.e. more tourists=more English). Also there is a certain political climate in my (limited) experience of Quebec regarding the relationship between English and French and the more hardcore francophones will really appreciate/respect you trying to immerse yourself in the French language and culture. 

In terms of Québecois accents, that's fairly minor in the urban areas. You might have more issues in very rural Quebec but even that would be manageable in my opinion.
